definitions.definition: I={i∈ℤ:0≤i≤λ}. Factorials and binomial coefficients with indices in this range are those of the corresponding nonnegative integers.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For each integer r≥0, X_r=x^r/r!, where powers denote composition of the action of x and X_0=Id_V.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For each integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r!, where powers denote composition of the action of y and Y_0=Id_V.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C), with its action on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers x^r/r!,y^r/r! for integers r≥0; their actions on V are X_r,Y_r.

definitions.type: subring of ℚ, also embedded in ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p does not divide b}, with the usual rational arithmetic and its embedding into ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Once its multiplication map into V is proved injective, it is identified with its image in V.
ι_R is the tensor multiplication map determined by ι_R(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R and m∈M, using the rational scalar action on V.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I×I
definitions.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero. This definition is made only after (e_k)_{k∈I} has been proved to be a complex basis of V.

inputs.statement: V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The elements x,y,h are its Chevalley generators and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. It is arbitrary and is not required to be the minimal lattice.

n=λ+1>0 and card(I)=n. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V; e_0=v. For every integer m≥0, h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v; for m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v. The vectors y^m v vanish for m>λ. The action matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix coefficients are integers.

output.statement: ι_R:M_R→V is injective, its image spans V over ℂ, and M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, of rank n. Every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves M and, under this embedding, also preserves M_R. For every integer t with 0≤t≤λ, t! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M and give its induced Chevalley action after tensoring.

locals.type: integer basis of M indexed by I, also a complex basis of V
locals.declaration: Choose an integer basis f=(f_i)_{i∈I} of M that is a complex basis of V, using F001.

argument.text: By H006 choose an integer basis of M that is also a complex basis of V. Its index set is finite because V has finite complex dimension (H004). M002 applied to this complex basis over ℂ counts its elements as dim_ℂ V=n. N001 gives card(I)=n, so reindexing gives an integer basis indexed by I. This proves F001. H001 ensures R is a subring: products of integers not divisible by the prime p are again not divisible by p, and addition and multiplication of the stated fractions preserve the denominator condition.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis of M indexed by I that is also a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Choose f as in F001. M001 with A=ℤ, B=R and T=M gives the R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Under ι_R these vectors go to f_i. If ∑ r_i f_i=0 with r_i∈R, complex independence of f gives every r_i=0. Hence ι_R is injective. Its image contains f and therefore spans V over ℂ. This also proves that M_R is free of rank n. From now on identify M_R with this image.

produces.statement: ι_R is injective; M_R has R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I}, has rank n, and its image spans V over ℂ.

argument.text: Admissibility H006 makes every X_r,Y_r preserve M; their complex linearity then preserves the R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=[x,y]=xy-yx does too by H004. These integral operators obey the Chevalley brackets on M and therefore induce the stated action after tensoring. For any 0≤t≤λ, H003 gives t<p; applying M006 with ℓ=p to this arbitrary t and H001 gives p coprime to t!, hence p does not divide t!. Thus 1/t!∈R and t! is a unit. In particular λ!, j!, (λ-j)! are units for j∈I. The integer identity binom(λ,j)j!(λ-j)!=λ! shows that binom(λ,j) is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ-j)!/λ!.

produces.statement: All X_r,Y_r preserve M_R, and x,y,h preserve M. For 0≤t≤λ, t! is a unit of R; for every j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit of R.

argument.text: Compute on the complex e-basis of N001. X_λ kills all e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ sends e_0 to e_λ with coefficient 1. Thus Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}. Also X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient 1, so X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}. For E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}, an input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by the projection; if k>j it is sent beyond the end of the string and is zero. On e_j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Thus E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. Composing gives E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Every factor preserves M_R by F003, and its scalar lies in R. Hence all E_ij preserve M_R. These identities and preservation statements require no distinction of weights modulo p.
